question: Your Agent SDK coordinator uses a codebase exploration subagent to study a legacy system and a boilerplate generation subagent to create new modules. The exploration subagent must record a short finding in a findings file many times per task, but it should never change source code. You are now deciding the allowedTools for each subagent. Which two configurations best follow scoped tool access?

options.text: Add a scoped append_finding tool to the exploration subagent that can only append a short entry to its findings file.
options.reason: A limited cross-role tool covers a specific high-frequency need, frequent note-taking, without giving the subagent the full Write tool.

options.text: Merge both subagents into one agent that holds every built-in tool, so the agent never needs a cross-role tool for its findings.
options.reason: This removes role scoping, and the guide says that agents with tools outside their specialization tend to misuse them.

options.text: Give each subagent every tool from the connected MCP servers, and rely on the tool descriptions to guide each subagent toward the right tools for its role.
options.reason: The guide says that too many tools degrade tool selection reliability, and scoped access means giving only the tools that the role needs.

options.text: Give the exploration subagent only Read, Grep, and Glob, and give the Write tool only to the generation subagent, which creates the new modules.
options.reason: Scoped tool access gives each agent only the tools that its role needs, so the read-only exploration role gets no general write access.

options.text: Give the exploration subagent the full Write tool, and set tool_choice to "any" so that it must call a tool on every turn.
options.reason: The "any" setting only guarantees that some tool is called, and the full Write tool still gives the exploration subagent access beyond its role.
